q: The first Indian to be awarded the Nobel Prize was:
e: Rabindranath Tagore, who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali, was the first Indian Nobel laureate.

q: The Strait of Malacca, one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, connects:

options.A: The Andaman Sea with the South China Sea
options.B: The Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden
options.C: The Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman
options.D: The Mediterranean Sea with the Black Sea

e: The Strait of Malacca connects the Andaman Sea with the South China Sea and is a vital shipping lane between the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

q: The Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system in the world, is located off the north-eastern coast of:
e: The Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system, lies off the north-eastern coast of Australia.

q: The largest and deepest ocean in the world is the:
e: The Pacific is the largest and deepest of the world's oceans, covering about one-third of the Earth's surface.

q: The Sahara, the largest hot desert in the world, is located in the continent of:
e: The Sahara, the largest hot desert in the world, stretches across northern Africa.

q: Lake Baikal, the deepest freshwater lake in the world, holding about one-fifth of the world's fresh surface water, is situated in:
e: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is the deepest freshwater lake in the world and holds about one-fifth of the world's fresh surface water.

q: The longest river of Europe is the:
e: The Volga, flowing through Russia into the Caspian Sea, is the longest river of Europe.

q: The Dead Sea, known for its exceptionally high salinity, is bordered by Israel and:
e: The Dead Sea, famous for its exceptionally high salinity, is bordered by Israel on one side and Jordan on the other.

q: The Karakoram Highway, one of the highest paved international roads in the world, connects Pakistan with:
e: The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with China across the Khunjerab Pass, one of the highest border crossings in the world.

q: In Tibet, the river Brahmaputra is known by the name:
e: In Tibet, the Brahmaputra is known as the Tsangpo (Yarlung Tsangpo) before it enters India.

q: The concept of Five-Year Plans in India was borrowed from the:
e: The concept of Five-Year Plans in India was borrowed from the former USSR, where centralised planning had been practised.

q: 'Inflation' in an economy refers to:

options.A: A fall in the general level of prices
options.B: An increase in the production of goods
options.C: A sustained rise in the general level of prices
options.D: A decrease in the supply of money

e: Inflation means a sustained rise in the general level of prices, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

q: The first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) in Asia was set up in India in 1965 at:
e: Asia's first Export Processing Zone was set up at Kandla in 1965 to promote export-oriented production.

q: A country is said to have a 'trade deficit' when:

options.A: The value of its imports exceeds the value of its exports
options.B: The value of its exports exceeds the value of its imports
options.C: Its government expenditure exceeds its revenue
options.D: Its foreign exchange reserves fall to zero

e: A trade deficit arises when the value of a country's imports exceeds the value of its exports.

q: The headquarters of UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) is located at:
e: UNESCO, the UN agency for education, science and culture, has its headquarters at Paris.

q: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India is compiled and released by the:

options.D: Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion

e: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is compiled and released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), MoSPI - the CSO was merged into the NSO. (Source: MoSPI order dated 23.05.2019 merging CSO and NSSO into the National Statistical Office.)

q: The 'Maharatna' status, which grants greater financial and operational autonomy, is conferred by the Government of India upon:
e: Maharatna status, carrying enhanced financial and operational autonomy, is conferred on top-performing Central Public Sector Enterprises.

q: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
e: The coulomb is the SI unit of electric charge; the ampere measures current, the volt potential difference and the ohm resistance.

q: The circulation of blood in the human body was first correctly described by:
e: William Harvey first correctly described the circulation of blood in the human body, in 1628.

q: The largest gland in the human body is the:
e: The liver is the largest gland in the human body, performing functions like bile production and metabolism.

q: The speed of sound in air at ordinary temperature is approximately:
e: The speed of sound in air at ordinary temperature is approximately 343 metres per second.

q: The Universal Law of Gravitation was propounded by:
e: The Universal Law of Gravitation, explaining the attraction between masses, was propounded by Isaac Newton.

q: The first human being to set foot on the Moon, in July 1969, was:
e: Neil Armstrong of Apollo 11 was the first human being to set foot on the Moon, in July 1969.

q: The largest mammal in the world is the:
e: The blue whale is the largest mammal, and indeed the largest known animal, in the world.

q: Hydrogen-filled balloons were replaced by balloons filled with helium mainly because helium is:
e: Helium replaced hydrogen in balloons because it is light like hydrogen but non-flammable, making it far safer.

q: The National Flag of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
e: The National Flag of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947, shortly before independence.

q: The National Calendar of India, used for official purposes, is based on the:
e: The National Calendar of India, adopted for official purposes, is based on the Saka Era.

q: International Literacy Day is observed every year on:
e: International Literacy Day, proclaimed by UNESCO, is observed every year on 8 September.

q: The Santosh Trophy is the premier championship in India for:
e: The Santosh Trophy is the premier inter-state championship in Indian football.

q: The Olympic Games were held in Asia for the first time in 1964 at:
e: The Olympic Games came to Asia for the first time in 1964, when they were hosted by Tokyo.

q: The Jodhpur division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Jodhpur division is one of the divisions of the North Western Railway, headquartered at Jaipur.

q: The Nanded division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Nanded division belongs to the South Central Railway, headquartered at Secunderabad.

q: The Mumbai CSMT division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Mumbai CSMT division is administered by the Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Mumbai CSMT itself.

q: The Shramjeevi Express, a superfast train of the Patna region, runs between Rajgir and:
e: The Shramjeevi Express runs between Rajgir in Bihar and New Delhi.

q: The Magadh Express runs between New Delhi and:
e: The Magadh Express links New Delhi with Islampur in Bihar.

q: The Kashi Vishwanath Express runs between Varanasi and:
e: The Kashi Vishwanath Express runs between Varanasi, the city of the Kashi Vishwanath temple, and New Delhi.

q: The Lichchhavi Express runs between Sitamarhi in Bihar and:
e: The Lichchhavi Express runs between Sitamarhi in Bihar and Anand Vihar Terminal in Delhi.

q: The Himgiri Express runs between Howrah and:
e: The Himgiri Express runs between Howrah and Jammu Tawi.

q: The Doon Express runs between Howrah and:
e: The Doon Express runs between Howrah and Dehradun, the gateway to the Doon valley.

q: The Bagh Express runs between Howrah and:
e: The Bagh Express runs between Howrah and Kathgodam, the railhead for the Kumaon hills.

q: The Kamrup Express runs between Howrah and:
e: The Kamrup Express runs between Howrah and Dibrugarh in upper Assam, taking its name from the Kamrup region.

q: The Vikramshila Express runs between Bhagalpur and:
e: The Vikramshila Express runs between Bhagalpur and Anand Vihar Terminal in Delhi.

q: The Mahakoshal Express runs between Jabalpur and:
e: The Mahakoshal Express runs between Jabalpur and Hazrat Nizamuddin in Delhi.

q: The Samta Express runs between Hazrat Nizamuddin (Delhi) and:
e: The Samta Express runs between Hazrat Nizamuddin in Delhi and Visakhapatnam.

q: The Ganga Kaveri Express runs between Chennai Central and:
e: The Ganga Kaveri Express runs between Chennai Central and Chhapra in Bihar.

q: The Rani Chennamma Express, named after the warrior queen of Kittur, runs between Bengaluru and:
e: The Rani Chennamma Express, named after the warrior queen of Kittur, runs between Bengaluru and Kolhapur.

q: The Lalbagh Express runs between Chennai Central and:
e: The Lalbagh Express runs between Chennai Central and Bengaluru.

q: The Pearl City Express runs between Chennai Egmore and:
e: The Pearl City Express runs between Chennai Egmore and Thoothukudi, which is known as the Pearl City for its pearl fishing.

q: The Sethu Express runs between Chennai Egmore and:
e: The Sethu Express runs between Chennai Egmore and Rameswaram, named after the legendary Sethu or bridge towards Lanka.

q: The Blue Mountain Express runs between Chennai Central and:
e: The Blue Mountain Express runs between Chennai Central and Mettupalayam, the base station for the Nilgiri or Blue Mountain line.

q: The Ajanta Express, named after the famous cave paintings, runs between Secunderabad and:
e: The Ajanta Express, named after the Ajanta caves, runs between Secunderabad and Manmad.

q: The Circar Express runs between Chennai Central and:
e: The Circar Express runs between Chennai Central and Kakinada Port in Andhra Pradesh.

q: The Kashi Mahakal Express, operated by IRCTC, runs between Varanasi and:
e: The IRCTC-operated Kashi Mahakal Express runs between Varanasi and Indore, linking the Jyotirlinga shrines on its route.

q: The Maveli Express runs between Thiruvananthapuram and:
e: The Maveli Express runs between Thiruvananthapuram and Mangaluru along the Kerala coast.

q: The Saryu Yamuna Express runs between Jaynagar in Bihar and:
e: The Saryu Yamuna Express runs between Jaynagar in Bihar and Amritsar in Punjab.

q: In Indian Railways, 'JTBS', the agents engaged to sell unreserved tickets at locations away from railway stations, stands for:
e: JTBS stands for Jan Sadharan Ticket Booking Sevak, the agents authorised to sell unreserved tickets away from station premises.

q: Under the 'VIKALP' scheme of Indian Railways, a waitlisted passenger is given the option of:

options.A: A refund of fare without any deduction
options.B: Upgradation to a higher class in the same train
options.C: Confirmed accommodation in an alternate train on the same route
options.D: Booking a Tatkal ticket without premium charges

e: Under VIKALP, a waitlisted passenger can opt to be allotted confirmed accommodation in an alternate train on the same route.

q: In the locomotive class designation YDM-4 of Indian Railways, the first letter 'Y' indicates that the locomotive is built for:
e: In locomotive class designations, the first letter denotes the gauge: Y in YDM-4 stands for metre gauge, just as W denotes broad gauge and Z narrow gauge.

q: In railway signalling, a 'track circuit' provided on a section of track is primarily used to:

options.A: Detect the presence of a train on that section of track
options.B: Supply power to the train lighting system
options.C: Measure the speed of a passing train

e: A track circuit uses the rails as an electrical circuit to detect the presence of a train on that section of track, forming the basis of automatic signalling.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'HRMS', used for human resource management of railway employees, stands for:
e: HRMS stands for Human Resource Management System, the application used for service records and other HR functions of railway employees.

q: The very first train run in India, in 1851, even before the regular passenger service of 1853, carried construction material for an aqueduct (the Solani aqueduct of the Ganga Canal) near the town of:
e: The first train run in India, in 1851, hauled construction material for the Solani aqueduct of the Ganga Canal near Roorkee.

q: The first electric locomotive built by the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works, rolled out in 1961, was named:
e: The first electric locomotive built by Chittaranjan Locomotive Works, rolled out in 1961, was named Lokmanya, after Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

q: BEML Limited, which manufactures railway coaches and metro cars, is a public sector undertaking under the:
e: BEML Limited, maker of railway coaches and metro cars, is a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Defence.

q: The Rail Spring Karkhana of Indian Railways, which manufactures helical and laminated springs for coaches and wagons, is located at:
e: The Rail Spring Karkhana, which makes helical and laminated springs for coaches and wagons, is located at Sithouli near Gwalior.

q: The Patiala Locomotive Works (PLW) at Patiala was earlier known as the:

options.A: Diesel Component Works only, since its inception

e: The Patiala Locomotive Works at Patiala was earlier known as the Diesel Loco Modernisation Works (DMW).

q: Special coaches or even a full train can be booked by the public from Indian Railways for tours, marriages and the like, on payment of the prescribed charges, which is known as booking on:
e: Special coaches or trains booked by the public for tours or functions on payment of full charges are booked on Full Tariff Rate (FTR).

q: The Jubilee Bridge, opened in 1887 and among the oldest railway bridges in India, was the first rail bridge built across which river?
e: The Jubilee Bridge, opened in 1887, was the first rail bridge across the Hooghly, linking the two banks near Kolkata.

q: The first transcontinental railroad of the United States was completed in 1869 when the famous 'Golden Spike' was driven at:
e: The first US transcontinental railroad was completed in 1869 when the Golden Spike was driven at Promontory Summit in Utah.

q: The 'Indian Pacific', one of the great long-distance trains of the world, runs across Australia between Sydney and:
e: The Indian Pacific runs across Australia between Sydney on the east coast and Perth on the west coast.

q: The 'Glacier Express', famous as one of the most scenic train journeys in the world and often called the slowest express train, runs in the country of:
e: The Glacier Express, a scenic panoramic train between Zermatt and St. Moritz, runs in Switzerland.

q: The first underground railway (subway) line in Asia was opened in 1927 in the city of:
e: Asia's first underground railway line was opened in Tokyo in 1927.

q: The high-speed trains known by the name 'TGV' are the famous trains of:
e: TGV, short for Train a Grande Vitesse, is the famous high-speed train system of France.

q: Grand Central Terminal, generally regarded as the largest railway station in the world by the number of platforms, is located in the city of:
e: Grand Central Terminal in New York is generally regarded as the largest railway station in the world by number of platforms.

q: The world's first commercial maglev (magnetic levitation) train service, opened in 2004 to link a city with its international airport, was started in:
e: The world's first commercial maglev service opened in 2004 in Shanghai, China, linking the city with Pudong International Airport.

q: The longest straight stretch of railway track in the world, running for about 478 km without a single curve, lies on the Trans-Australian Railway across which plain of Australia?
e: The longest straight stretch of track in the world, about 478 km without a curve, crosses the Nullarbor Plain on the Trans-Australian Railway.

q: Which Article of the Constitution declares that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in the Devanagari script?
e: Article 343 declares that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in the Devanagari script.

q: A Proclamation of Financial Emergency under Article 360 of the Constitution has so far been issued in India:
e: A Proclamation of Financial Emergency under Article 360 has never been issued in India so far, though the provision exists in the Constitution.

q: The writ of 'Habeas Corpus', issued by a court for the protection of personal liberty, literally means:

options.A: To have the body (to produce the person before the court)

e: Habeas corpus literally means "to have the body", the writ by which a court orders a detained person to be produced before it to protect personal liberty.

q: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 relates to:
e: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to Municipalities, the urban local self-government bodies.

q: By the 91st Constitutional Amendment, the total number of Ministers in the Union Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed what percentage of the total strength of the Lok Sabha?
e: The 91st Amendment capped the Union Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, at 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

q: The Constituent Assembly of India held its first meeting on:
e: The Constituent Assembly of India held its first meeting on 9 December 1946.

q: The Estimates Committee, the largest committee of the Indian Parliament, consists of how many members?
e: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, making it the largest committee of Parliament.

q: The Zonal Councils in India are:

options.A: Constitutional bodies set up under Article 263
options.B: Bodies set up by a resolution of the Union Cabinet
options.C: Bodies provided for in the Seventh Schedule
options.D: Statutory bodies set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956

e: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, to promote inter-state cooperation.

q: Who was the first Viceroy of India under the British Crown?
e: Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India in 1858, when the Crown took over from the East India Company.

q: Under the Charter Act of 1833, the first Governor-General of India was:
e: Under the Charter Act of 1833, Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India, having earlier been Governor-General of Bengal.

q: The Cripps Mission, which brought constitutional proposals to India during the Second World War, came to India in the year:
e: The Cripps Mission came to India in 1942, during the Second World War, offering constitutional proposals that were rejected by Indian leaders.

q: The ancient site of Harappa of the Indus Valley Civilisation was first excavated in 1921 under the supervision of:
e: Harappa was first excavated in 1921 under the supervision of Daya Ram Sahni.

q: The Magna Carta, the historic charter of liberties granted by King John of England, was signed in the year:
e: The Magna Carta, the historic charter of liberties, was granted by King John of England in 1215.

q: The French Revolution of 1789 began with the storming of the:
e: The French Revolution of 1789 began with the storming of the Bastille prison in Paris on 14 July 1789.

q: The first President of the United States of America was:
e: George Washington, commander of the Continental Army in the American Revolution, was the first President of the United States.

q: Christopher Columbus reached the Americas (the 'New World') in the year:
e: Christopher Columbus reached the Americas in 1492, on a voyage sponsored by Spain.

q: The printing press with movable type, which revolutionised the spread of books in Europe, was developed by:
e: Johannes Gutenberg developed the printing press with movable type in Europe, revolutionising the spread of books.

q: Which river is popularly known as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (the Ganga of the South)?
e: The Godavari, the largest river of peninsular India, is popularly known as the Dakshin Ganga, the Ganga of the South.

q: The Vembanad Lake, the longest lake in India, is located in the State of:
e: Vembanad Lake, the longest lake in India, is located in Kerala.

q: The International Date Line, on crossing which the calendar date changes, roughly follows the:
e: The International Date Line roughly follows the 180 degree longitude, where the calendar date changes on crossing it.

q: The Bering Strait separates the continents of:
e: The Bering Strait separates Asia (Russia) from North America (Alaska).

q: The longest river of Asia is the:
e: The Yangtze, flowing across China, is the longest river of Asia.

q: Angel Falls, the highest waterfall in the world, is located in:
e: Angel Falls, the highest waterfall in the world, is located in Venezuela.

q: The largest country in the world by area is:
e: Russia is the largest country in the world by area, spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.

q: 'El Nino', which influences the monsoon rainfall in India, refers to:

options.A: A cold ocean current in the Atlantic Ocean
options.B: The periodic warming of the surface waters of the Pacific Ocean
options.C: A tropical cyclone in the Bay of Bengal
options.D: A high-pressure system over the Indian Ocean

e: El Nino is the periodic warming of the surface waters of the eastern Pacific Ocean, which weakens the Indian monsoon in many years.
